title: Kenya mobile money (M-PESA)
summary: The original mobile-money system, still the reference model for emerging-market finance.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

M-PESA launched in Kenya in 2007 as a way to send money by SMS and became the country's dominant payment and store-of-value system, long before smartphones. It proved that a mobile network, an agent network and simple regulation could bank the unbanked. Newer systems in Africa and Asia copy the agent-based model rather than the app-based one.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Mass production
Estimated window 2007–2030
Confidence label Confirmed
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

The lesson for fintech is that distribution through local agents beats app elegance where cash is still the alternative.

What Would Change The View

  • Interoperability with bank rails.
  • Regulatory oversight of agent float.
  • Competition from smartphone-based wallets.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
